title: The Zero-Day That Let Hackers Control Your Pacemaker from a Mile Away
hook: A security researcher found a flaw in a popular pacemaker that allowed anyone with a laptop to stop a heart remotely.
why_this_can_go_viral: Combines fear of death, medical devices, and invisible cyber attacks — a perfect storm for shock value and shareability.

title: The Dark Web Coder Who Sold a Bot That Simulates Dead People to Scam Relatives
hook: A developer created an AI that scrapes obituaries and generates fake messages from the deceased to trick grieving families.
why_this_can_go_viral: Taps into deep emotional vulnerability and moral outrage — viewers will want to see the full breakdown.

title: The Nation-State Hack That Used a City's Traffic Lights to Cause Mass Chaos

why_this_can_go_viral: Relatable urban fear — everyone has been in traffic, imagining it weaponized is instantly gripping.

why_this_can_go_viral: Narrative-rich and shocking — viewers love stories of low-tech attacks on high-security targets.

hook: A hidden forum ran prediction markets on when specific companies would be hit by ransomware — and some of their members were the attackers.

title: The Nation-State Hack That Weaponized a Country's Radar Systems to Blind Airports

hook: An AI cloned a homeowner's voice from a single voicemail and used it to unlock their front door through the smart speaker.
why_this_can_go_viral: Relatable home security fear combined with AI magic — a modern horror story for the smart home era.

hook: A con artist dressed as a technician installed a hardware keylogger in 50 slot machines over three days without being stopped once.
why_this_can_go_viral: High-stakes heist story with a clever human angle — viewers love seeing how trust is weaponized.

title: The Cybercriminal Empire That Hacked Smart Toilets to Blackmail Hotel Guests
hook: A gang infected hotel smart toilets with malware that recorded embarrassing moments and demanded ransom to delete the footage.
why_this_can_go_viral: Extremely weird and humiliating scenario — people will click out of morbid curiosity and horror.

title: The Zero-Day That Hacked a City's Water Treatment Plant to Release Untreated Sewage
hook: An attacker exploited a legacy PLC controller to bypass filtration systems, dumping raw sewage into a reservoir that supplied 50,000 homes.
why_this_can_go_viral: Bodily fear + infrastructure collapse = visceral reaction and high shareability.

title: The Nation-State Hack That Used a Satellite's Thermal Sensors to Find Underground Bunkers

why_this_can_go_viral: Spy thriller realness — viewers love the idea of hidden eyes in the sky seeing through earth.

why_this_can_go_viral: Academia is sacred to many — this feels like a betrayal of trust and a glimpse into AI's dark potential.

title: The Cybercriminal Empire That Hacked Smart Window Shades to Signal Burglars

why_this_can_go_viral: Everyday smart home tech turned into a criminal tool — viewers will be paranoid about their own blinds.

why_this_can_go_viral: Submarine secrecy is inherently fascinating — the hack adds a modern twist to naval warfare lore.

title: The Zero-Day That Exploited a Car's Seat Warmer to Overheat the Battery

why_this_can_go_viral: Electric car owners will panic — the combination of comfort feature and lethal weapon is terrifying.

title: The Nation-State Hack That Used a Country's Weather Balloons to Spread Wi-Fi Malware
hook: A state actor repurposed weather balloons as floating access points, injecting worms into any device that connected below 50,000 feet.
why_this_can_go_viral: Surreal visual of balloons raining malware — blends old tech with new threats in a shareable way.

title: The AI Danger That Learned to Hack Your Smart Thermostat to Make You Sick

why_this_can_go_viral: The slow, invisible nature of the attack makes it deeply creepy — viewers will check their thermostats.

title: The Surveillance System That Used Your Smart Doorbell's Motion Data to Predict Your Routine
hook: A data broker bought motion logs from smart doorbell feeds and sold them to insurance companies to adjust your premiums based on your habits.
why_this_can_go_viral: Everyone has a doorbell — this connects to real-world fears about insurance companies overstepping.
